relationships.description: Factory initializer allocates0x30 bytes, constructs FileSystem, stores actual primary pointer at factory+14
FileSystem+8 receives factory+4 volume manager; +c/+10/+14 receive factory+8/+c/+10 secondary +4 aliases when non-null
Initializer allocates/zeros backend pointer array; mount path calls selector to bind selected secondary interface and may clear it on mount failure
signed descriptor+14==4 selects Virtual; else unsigned descriptor+18>0403ffff selects ExFat, else Fat. Fields are not named as size or sectors.
Open creates eight-byte wrapper{raw lower handle,index}; read uses wrapper+4 to choose backend and wrapper+0 as lower handle
FAT read directly calls533681c4; exFAT read directly calls5337f554. Lower library/OS transport not traced or executed.

Open after successful wrapper allocation and close normalize lower0 to0 and lower nonzero to1. Read and stat preserve the lower32-bit result. Synthetic statuses0,1,2,ffffffff prove the distinction; they do not establish backend error conventions.

limitations: No actual filesystem/IPC/storage IO, updater acceptance or hardware operation.
Factory initializer top-level task/startup caller is not resolved in this bounded pass; producer is grounded in its vtable entry and body.
Backend selection is conditional on established factory/volume objects and mount policy; actual update path first byte and mounted medium are not established.
descriptor+14 and+18 meanings remain numeric fields; no physical media/sector/byte labeling inferred.
49 CPU cases use synthetic volume descriptors, backend callbacks, allocator, lock and assertion boundaries; factory is a fragment, not full startup.
Facade read/stat do not gate lower calls on their inner lock return; outer loader mutex gate is distinct. No concurrency failure claim.
Lower FAT/exFAT direct calls are software boundaries only; names do not establish syscall or physical driver behavior.
Genuine angr C is unedited automatic analysis and may contain conditional/type artifacts; original ARM and pinned CPU checks govern claims.
